+# V4.1 integration snapshot
+
+This branch assembles the V4.1 text training components for evaluation. Start with
+[the training guide](examples/deepseek_v41/README.md). The training entrypoint is
+`pretrain_hybrid.py`; the model uses `--dsv4-version v4.1` and physical `VE` layer
+pairs. Model weights and tokenizer-derived Engram maps are not included.
+
+## Included components
+
+| Component | Upstream PR |
+| --- | --- |
+| Generic cross-layer tensor state, checkpointing, graphs and PP/VPP transport | [#7678](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/7678) |
+| Single-pass mHC and parameter-publication readiness | [#8223](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8223) |
+| CSA2 Full/Reindex/Reuse, candidate indexing and MXFP8 selection | [#8224](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8224) |
+| V4.1 Engram on shared EP embedding tables | [#8225](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8225) |
+| V4.1 model composition and FP8 recompute/capture integration | [#8226](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8226) |
+| Training builder and static packed pipeline scheduling | [#8227](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8227) |
+| Optional Mixture-of-Kittens MoE backend | [#8210](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8210) |
+
+The MoK dependency is pinned to the code from PR #8210 at
+`077837249a1f128ca02cf58f9fca2ebc180e8fb8`, plus the small configuration guard that
+keeps native HybridEP padding requirements out of MoK dispatch. Newer revisions
+of that PR are not part of this validated snapshot. The MoK guard remains an
+integration follow-up owned by the MoK effort.
+
+This is an integration snapshot, not a new pull request or a released-model
+convergence claim. Component PRs retain their separate review boundaries. The
+production and test files are identical to the validated integrated commit
+`4fe0301dfccf5a3d689d2efc7cf5476a81be475f`; publication only reorganizes commit
+ancestry and updates documentation.
+
+## Validation scope
+
+The integrated stack completed BF16 and MXFP8 training on 16 GB200 GPUs with
+TP1/PP2/VPP4/EP8/CP4, 24 logical blocks, 48 experts, 16K packed documents, MBS1 and
+GBS128. The recipe uses distributed Muon, MoK, selective MLA-up-projection/mHC
+recomputation and overlapped gradient reduction/parameter gather. Engram and
+CUDA graphs are disabled in this performance recipe.
+
+Each run completed 12 iterations with no skipped or non-finite logged steps.
+Using the median of iterations 3–12 and the same model-FLOPs convention:
+
+| Precision | Seconds/step | Model TFLOPS/GPU | Peak PyTorch allocated memory |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| BF16 | 27.28 | 308.5 | 128.2 GiB |
+| MXFP8 | 29.09 | 289.3 | 117.4 GiB |
+
+These are proxy measurements in the recorded GB200 environment, not full-model
+performance or a hardware-counter measurement. PyTorch allocated memory excludes
+external CUDA allocations. The tested software stack used PyTorch nv26.09,
+Transformer Engine 2.20.2 and cuDNN Frontend 1.29.
+
+Separate small-configuration checks cover MXFP8 selection, packed/CP boundaries,
+explicit graph replay, recomputation, PP and Engram/EP. They do not establish
+full-model, same-weight cross-branch gradient equivalence. Supported execution
+boundaries and remaining exclusions are described in the training guide.

A GTP_remat-replicated whole param (e.g. MoE router, latent-proj MLPs by default) then lands on one checkpoint key shared by all GTP_remat peers, so the LayerWise optimizer folds `gtp_rank` into its `replica_id` — exactly one peer writes (the optimizer-state analog of the model-side fold in §3.3).
 - **Split-QKV is layout-invariant.** Muon orthogonalizes a fused `linear_qkv` weight as separate **q**, **k** and **v** blocks, and *whether* it does must not depend on the parallel layout. Splitting and not splitting are **two different update rules**, not small perturbations of one: q is typically far larger than k and v, so orthogonalizing the fused matrix lets q dominate the spectrum the k and v rows are scaled by. Newton–Schulz is a nonlinear iteration, so the gap compounds over steps rather than averaging out — the same weight would train differently at TP1 than under GTP_remat.

-  - **`auto` is pinned to `duplicated`** whenever a split is requested, since its shape-based cost model has no notion of `qkv_split_shapes` and could otherwise drop the split on some shapes and keep it on others.
-  - **`blockwise` and `distributed`, chosen explicitly, fall back** to whole-matrix Newton–Schulz and **warn once**, since neither keeps a q/k/v boundary. `duplicated`, the default, is the path that gets the split.

+The same JSON controls row parallelism and the optional lookup runtime. For a
+128-rank physical stage (TP1), the following fields shard Engram over all 128
+ranks independently of MoE EP64:
+
+```json
+{
+  "parallel_size": 128,
+  "prefetch": true,
+  "defer_grad_transfer": true,
+  "buffer_budget_mb": 1024,
+  "communication_backend": "hybridep",
+  "hybridep_chunk_size": 32768
+}
+```
+
+Merge these fields into the existing architecture JSON. `parallel_size` must
+divide the physical stage's DP×CP size; the remaining factor is the number of
+table replicas. The builder creates the groups once, and the parameter domain
+carries them through DDP, optimizer ownership, Sinkhorn statistics and checkpoint
+replica metadata. Independent row parallelism currently requires TP1, no GTP
+remapping, standard Megatron DDP and one distributed optimizer instance. Use
+LayerWise for Muon/Sinkhorn, or DistributedOptimizer for Adam/SGD. When changing
+from the legacy expert optimizer domain to the new `engram` domain, load model
+weights with a fresh optimizer; automatic migration of legacy optimizer groups
+is not implemented.
+
+Omitting `parallel_size` preserves the existing EP/expert-DP partition and
+optimizer domain. `prefetch` and `defer_grad_transfer` default to false and can
+be enabled independently. The original lookup remains available when both are
+off with the NCCL or HybridEP backend. Prefetch stages token/THD metadata before
+the PP schedule, shares it across VPP chunks, deduplicates each batch's requests,
+and carries a ticket to the matching consumer. Lookup runs outside full
+recomputation and partial CUDA graphs; projection and gating retain their normal
+recompute behavior. Deferred backward coalesces queued microbatches per table,
+delivers row gradients to their owners, then lets DDP reduce replicas.
+
+`buffer_budget_mb` bounds the runtime's reserved row-payload/gradient capacity,
+shared across local tables and VPP chunks. Pressure flushes pending gradients
+and evicts optional prefetch payloads, which can be fetched again. It does not
+bound model activations, saved request routes, transient tensor operations,
+DDP/optimizer storage or opaque NCCL/HybridEP allocations. A single lookup that
+cannot fit raises an error requesting a larger budget; rows are never dropped.
+
+The experimental `communication_backend: "symmetric"` binds NCCL4Py + CuTe DSL.
+Within an NCCL LSA domain it reads registered table rows directly. Cross-domain
+requests, packed FP8 bytes/scales and gradients use GIN. Two receive slots per
+sender bound staging memory; GPU completion signals protect slot reuse, without
+per-chunk host launches or collectives. The existing Triton activation repack is
+reused; sorted duplicate gradients are accumulated by one Triton writer per row.
+Count planning and table-registration metadata still use host collectives per
+lookup. Registration is reused while parameter storage is unchanged,
+and collectively refreshed if an optimizer/DDP operation replaces an allocation.
+
+This requires `nccl4py >= 0.6.0`, CuTe DSL, and matching NCCL headers/runtime/device
+bitcode. Prefer CuTe DSL 4.8.1: its
+[release notes](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#481-2026-10-15)
+confirm the fix for zero-argument `cute.extern` calls across compilations.
+Unmodified 4.8.0 can fail repeated NCCL barrier compilation with an MLIR context
+mismatch. The isolated extern recompilation check passes with unmodified 4.8.1.
+Four-GPU B300 smoke tests have passed with CuTe DSL 4.7.0,
+NCCL4Py 0.6.0 and NCCL 2.32.3.
+If setting `NCCL_HOME`, it must identify that same NCCL installation with
+`lib/libnccl_device.bc`.
+Cross-domain operation requires full-peer GIN connectivity; LSA-only groups do
+not require GIN. Table allocations must be registerable CUDA VMM memory, e.g.
+`PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True`; tables are never shadow-copied.
+PyTorch storage starts need not be 4-KiB aligned. Window registration queries the
+underlying CUDA mapping, registers from its base, and records each table's full
+offset from that window so LSA reads handle different suballocations on peers.
+The borrowed window buffer retains the original storage;
+allocation queries and registration are cached until storage changes.
+Workspace is included in `buffer_budget_mb`; NCCL's internal allocations are not.
+Use `EngramRuntime.close()` before destroying the row groups when explicitly
+tearing down a model. Single-node LSA exchange, direct reads, storage replacement,
+and MXFP8 prefetch/deferred-gradient/DDP integration have GPU smoke coverage.
+Cross-domain GIN, larger shard groups, and performance still need qualification
+in the target image.
+
 For PP/VPP, insert `|` at explicit stage/chunk boundaries. The builder creates
 one typed pipeline control group per replica and reuses it for virtual chunks.

 SFT packed loader, `--dataloader-inter-document-masking`, or static varlen
 scheduling with `--use-varlen-dataset --sequence-packing-scheduler dp_balanced`.

+For V4.1 head-wise Muon, enable `--muon-split-qkv-per-head` with the default
+QKV splitting enabled and `--muon-tp-mode duplicated`. The attention Q projection
+and Full/Reindex indexer Q projections split by their own head counts, including
+the full content and RoPE width of each head. SWA KV and the Full owner's indexer
+K each have one shared head and remain whole matrices. Reuse layers have no
+indexer weights. Output, compressor and other linear weights retain whole-matrix
+Muon. Without the per-head flag, V4.1 retains whole-projection updates.
+
+This also applies with `--use-layer-wise-distributed-optimizer`, which distributes
+whole parameters across DP ranks. The separate `--muon-tp-mode layer_sharded`
+algorithm currently rejects split-QKV/per-head Muon. GPU validation of V4.1
+per-head updates with distributed optimizer, FP8 parameter gather and checkpoint
+resume is still required; the training results above predate per-head support.
+
+For the paper's embedding/prediction-head update, add `--muon-use-sinkhorn` to
+`--optimizer muon` (also supported with `adaptive_muon`). This requires EO's
+`emerging_optimizers.orthogonalized_optimizers.sinkhorn_utils.sinkhorn_balance`;
+early builds with the same `0.5.0a0` version string may not include it. Linear
+weights continue to use Muon; norms, biases and other excluded parameters continue
+to use `--muon-scalar-optimizer`. Per-head Muon is independent of this flag.
+
+Sinkhorn uses EMA/Nesterov momentum 0.95, 11 alternating row/column L2
+normalizations ending on rows, a zero-row threshold of 1e-3, epsilon 1e-20 and
+update RMS 0.18 (`--sinkhorn-momentum`, `--sinkhorn-num-normalization-steps`,
+`--sinkhorn-zero-row-threshold`, `--sinkhorn-eps`, `--sinkhorn-extra-scale-factor`).
+Its groups always have zero weight decay, including under the weight-decay
+scheduler, and otherwise follow the embedding/output learning-rate schedule.
+
+V4.1 Engram lookup tables use a 5x learning-rate multiplier by default. Set

+disables the multiplier). Projections and normalization weights keep the base

+nonzero warmup and minimum LR, and is retained in optimizer checkpoints.

+e4m3` uses TE Linear for its fused key/value projection. Adding `--fp8-param-gather`
+also stores the lookup table in rowwise MXFP8; use

+keep BF16 Engram storage and projections too.

+those bytes as the projection's rowwise GEMM input. The table stores only one
+scaling direction. Projection weight gradients need columnwise quantization of
+the retrieved batch. Triton kernels gather values/scales directly into the EP
+payload, then fuse receive reordering, head concatenation and columnwise
+requantization into TE's GEMM buffers without an intermediate BF16 activation.

+through the model dtype as TE does. The single-table path skips table sorting.
+A native fallback remains available when Triton is absent, generating only the
+needed columnwise quantization. There is no persistent BF16 table or full-table
+columnwise copy. Lookup gradients

+the model gradient dtype. Normalization and gate arithmetic remain FP32.

+inference reference's 32-by-32 weight scaling layout.

+metadata and EP/replica-DP Sinkhorn parity. Blackwell tests cover real TE storage,
+fused/native payload and activation parity, projection gradients, recompute,
+optimizer copy-back and EP1/EP2 bit-exact replay (including fused scale padding).
+The latter tests require GPU qualification; they were not run on the CPU
+development host.

+"""Compact narrow CP compressor projections with a unique-source backward map."""
+
+import torch
+from torch import Tensor
+
+
+def cp_projection_maps(source_indices, valid_groups, full_halo_rows, halo_rows, local_rows):
+    """Build shared forward/inverse maps, excluding all logically padded groups.
+
+    Compression groups do not overlap for CSA2 r1/r2. Each participating source
+    therefore has exactly one compact row, so backward gathers instead of using
+    an atomic scatter. Invalid compact rows never overwrite a real inverse entry.
+    """
+    sources = source_indices.flatten() - (full_halo_rows - halo_rows)
+    valid = valid_groups[:, None].expand_as(source_indices).flatten()
+    sources = sources.masked_fill(~valid, -1)
+    inverse = torch.full((halo_rows + local_rows,), -1, dtype=torch.int64, device=sources.device)
+    rows = torch.arange(sources.numel(), device=sources.device).masked_fill(~valid, -1)
+    if inverse.numel():
+        inverse.scatter_reduce_(0, sources.clamp_min(0), rows, reduce="amax", include_self=True)
+    return sources, inverse
+
+
+def _compact_projection(local, halo, sources):
+    rows = sources - halo.shape[0]
+    shape = (-1,) + (1,) * (local.ndim - 1)
+    if local.shape[0] == 0 and halo.shape[0] == 0:
+        return local.new_zeros((sources.numel(), *local.shape[1:]))
+    if local.shape[0] == 0:
+        values = halo.index_select(0, sources.clamp(0, halo.shape[0] - 1))
+    elif halo.shape[0] == 0:
+        values = local.index_select(0, rows.clamp(0, local.shape[0] - 1))
+    else:
+        values = torch.where(
+            (rows < 0).reshape(shape),
+            halo.index_select(0, sources.clamp(0, halo.shape[0] - 1)),
+            local.index_select(0, rows.clamp(0, local.shape[0] - 1)),
+        )
+    return values.masked_fill((sources < 0).reshape(shape), 0)
+
+
+def _restore_projection_gradient(gradient, inverse):
+    if gradient.shape[0] == 0:
+        return gradient.new_zeros((inverse.numel(), *gradient.shape[1:]))
+    shape = (-1,) + (1,) * (gradient.ndim - 1)
+    return gradient.index_select(0, inverse.clamp_min(0)).masked_fill(
+        (inverse < 0).reshape(shape), 0
+    )
+
+
+_compiled_compact = torch.compile(_compact_projection, fullgraph=True)
+_compiled_restore = torch.compile(_restore_projection_gradient, fullgraph=True)
+
+
+class _CompactCPProjection(torch.autograd.Function):
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, local, halo, sources, inverse):
+        ctx.save_for_backward(inverse)
+        ctx.halo_rows = halo.shape[0]
+        implementation = _compiled_compact if local.is_cuda else _compact_projection
+        return implementation(local, halo, sources)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, gradient):
+        (inverse,) = ctx.saved_tensors
+        implementation = _compiled_restore if gradient.is_cuda else _restore_projection_gradient
+        restored = implementation(gradient, inverse)
+        halo, local = restored.split((ctx.halo_rows, inverse.numel() - ctx.halo_rows))
+        return local, halo, None, None
+
+
+def compact_cp_projection(local: Tensor, halo: Tensor, sources: Tensor, inverse: Tensor) -> Tensor:
+    """Compact projected KV or gate, saving only the shared integer inverse map."""
+    return _CompactCPProjection.apply(local, halo, sources, inverse)

+        recv_begin, recv_count = splits[recv_peer, 2], splits[recv_peer, 3]
+        if cutlass.const_expr(remote_only):
+            if send_local:
+                send_count = cutlass.Int64(0)
+            if recv_local:
+                recv_count = cutlass.Int64(0)
+        if offset == 0:
+            _copy_words(
+                cute.make_tensor(source.iterator + send_begin * row_words, source.layout),
+                cute.make_tensor(destination.iterator + recv_begin * row_words, destination.layout),
+                send_count * row_words,
+            )
+        else:
+            send_chunks = (send_count + capacity - 1) // capacity
+            recv_chunks = (recv_count + capacity - 1) // capacity
+            rounds = max(send_chunks, recv_chunks)
+            # Send n while consuming n-1. Two slots let the next put overlap the
+            # previous receive copy without a per-chunk host launch or collective.
+            for chunk in range(rounds + 1):
+                slot = chunk % 2
+                if chunk < send_chunks:
+                    ack = send_peer * 4 + 2 + slot
+                    expected_ack = sequence[ack]
+                    cute.arch.sync_threads()
+                    if send_local:
+                        _wait_lsa(window, ack, expected_ack, flags_offset)
+                    elif cutlass.const_expr(has_gin):
+                        gin.wait_signal(coop, signal=ack, least=expected_ack)
+                    count = min(capacity, send_count - chunk * capacity) * row_words
+                    src = cute.make_tensor(
+                        source.iterator + (send_begin + chunk * capacity) * row_words,
+                        cute.make_layout(count),
+                    )
+                    recv_offset = (2 * channels + 2 * team.rank + slot) * slot_bytes
+                    ready = team.rank * 4 + slot
+                    if send_local:
+                        dst = cute.make_tensor(
+                            cute.make_ptr(
+                                source.element_type, window.lsa_pointer(recv_offset, send_lsa)
+                            ),
+                            cute.make_layout(count),
+                        )
+                        _copy_words(src, dst, count)
+                        _signal_lsa(window, send_lsa, ready, flags_offset)
+                    elif cutlass.const_expr(has_gin):
+                        staging = window.tensor(
+                            source.element_type,
+                            cute.make_layout(count),
+                            offset=(2 * channel + slot) * slot_bytes,
+                        )
+                        _copy_words(src, staging, count)
+                        cute.arch.sync_threads()
+                        dst = window.tensor(
+                            source.element_type, cute.make_layout(count), offset=recv_offset
+                        )
+                        gin.put(
+                            team,
+                            send_peer,
+                            window,
+                            dst,
+                            window,
+                            staging,
+                            coop,
+                            is_signal=True,
+                            signal_id=ready,
+                            signal_op=0,
+                        )
+                    if tid == 0:
+                        sequence[ack] = expected_ack + 1
+                    cute.arch.sync_threads()
+                received_chunk = chunk - 1
+                if (received_chunk >= 0) & (received_chunk < recv_chunks):
+                    recv_slot = received_chunk % 2
+                    ready = recv_peer * 4 + recv_slot
+                    expected_ready = sequence[ready] + 1
+                    cute.arch.sync_threads()
+                    if recv_local:
+                        _wait_lsa(window, ready, expected_ready, flags_offset)
+                    elif cutlass.const_expr(has_gin):
+                        gin.wait_signal(coop, signal=ready, least=expected_ready)
+                    count = min(capacity, recv_count - received_chunk * capacity) * row_words
+                    src = window.tensor(
+                        source.element_type,
+                        cute.make_layout(count),
+                        offset=(2 * channels + 2 * recv_peer + recv_slot) * slot_bytes,
+                    )
+                    dst = cute.make_tensor(
+                        destination.iterator + (recv_begin + received_chunk * capacity) * row_words,
+                        cute.make_layout(count),
+                    )
+                    _copy_words(src, dst, count)
+                    cute.arch.sync_threads()
+                    ack = team.rank * 4 + 2 + recv_slot
+                    if recv_local:
+                        _signal_lsa(window, recv_lsa, ack, flags_offset)
+                    elif cutlass.const_expr(has_gin):
+                        gin.signal(team, recv_peer, True, ack, 0, 0, coop)
+                    if tid == 0:
+                        sequence[ready] = expected_ready
+                    cute.arch.sync_threads()
+            # Drain both outgoing slots, including the final partially filled one.
+            # The next exchange may change row width and peer counts.
+            for slot in cutlass.range_constexpr(2):
+                if slot < send_chunks:
+                    ack = send_peer * 4 + 2 + slot
+                    if send_local:
+                        _wait_lsa(window, ack, sequence[ack], flags_offset)
+                    elif cutlass.const_expr(has_gin):
+                        gin.wait_signal(coop, signal=ack, least=sequence[ack])
+    if cutlass.const_expr(has_gin):
+        gin.flush(coop)
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _exchange(
+    comm: nc.DevComm,
+    window: nc.Window,
+    source: cute.Tensor,
+    destination: cute.Tensor,
+    splits: cute.Tensor,
+    sequence: cute.Tensor,
+    slot_bytes: cutlass.Int64,
+    flags_offset: cutlass.Int64,
+    row_words: cutlass.Int64,
+    channels: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    has_gin: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    remote_only: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    stream: cuda.CUstream,
+):
+    _exchange_kernel(
+        comm,
+        window,
+        source,
+        destination,
+        splits,
+        sequence,
+        slot_bytes,
+        flags_offset,
+        row_words,
+        channels,
+        has_gin,
+        remote_only,
+    ).launch(grid=(channels, 1, 1), block=(128, 1, 1), stream=stream)
+

+@cute.kernel
+def _table_barrier_kernel(comm: nc.DevComm, has_gin: cutlass.Constexpr):
+    coop = nc.cta()
+    if cutlass.const_expr(has_gin):
+        gin = comm.gin(nc.GinBackendMask.ALL, 0)
+        barrier = nc.barrier.world_hybrid(coop, gin, comm, 0)
+        barrier.sync(coop, nc.MemoryOrder.ACQ_REL, nc.GinFenceLevel.NONE)
+        barrier.destroy()
+    else:
+        barrier = nc.barrier.lsa_default(coop, comm, 0)
+        barrier.sync(coop, nc.MemoryOrder.ACQ_REL)
+        barrier.destroy()
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _table_barrier(comm: nc.DevComm, has_gin: cutlass.Constexpr, stream: cuda.CUstream):
+    _table_barrier_kernel(comm, has_gin).launch(grid=(1, 1, 1), block=(128, 1, 1), stream=stream)
+
+
+@cute.kernel
+def _lookup_kernel(
+    comm: nc.DevComm,
+    data_windows: tuple,
+    scale_windows: tuple,
+    metadata: cute.Tensor,
+    requests: cute.Tensor,
+    peers: cute.Tensor,
+    output: cute.Tensor,
+    rows: cutlass.Int64,
+    data_words: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    scale_words: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    local_requests: cutlass.Constexpr,
+):
+    """Direct LSA reads, or owner-side packing of requests received over GIN."""
+    block, _, _ = cute.arch.block_idx()
+    tid, _, _ = cute.arch.thread_idx()
+    team, lsa = comm.team_world, comm.team_lsa
+    lsa_start = team.rank - lsa.rank
+    # Four warps per CTA, one row per warp; adjacent lanes read adjacent words.
+    row = block * 4 + tid // 32
+    lane = tid % 32
+    if row < rows:
+        peer = peers[row]
+        lsa_peer = peer - lsa_start
+        is_local = (lsa_peer >= 0) & (lsa_peer < lsa.nRanks)
+        valid = is_local
+        if cutlass.const_expr(not local_requests):
+            valid = not is_local
+            peer = team.rank
+            lsa_peer = lsa.rank
+        if valid:
+            table_id, table_row = requests[row * 2], requests[row * 2 + 1]
+            for table in cutlass.range_constexpr(len(data_windows)):
+                if table_id == table:
+                    data_offset = metadata[table, peer, 0] + table_row * metadata[table, peer, 1]
+                    data = cute.make_tensor(
+                        cute.make_ptr(
+                            output.element_type,
+                            data_windows[table].lsa_pointer(data_offset, lsa_peer),
+                        ),
+                        cute.make_layout(data_words),
+                    )
+                    for col in range(lane, data_words, 32):
+                        output[row * (data_words + scale_words) + col] = data[col]
+                    if cutlass.const_expr(scale_words > 0):
+                        scale_offset = (
+                            metadata[table, peer, 2] + table_row * metadata[table, peer, 3]
+                        )
+                        scales = cute.make_tensor(
+                            cute.make_ptr(
+                                output.element_type,
+                                scale_windows[table].lsa_pointer(scale_offset, lsa_peer),
+                            ),
+                            cute.make_layout(scale_words),
+                        )
+                        for col in range(lane, scale_words, 32):
+                            output[row * (data_words + scale_words) + data_words + col] = scales[
+                                col
+                            ]
+
+
+@cute.jit
+def _lookup(
+    comm: nc.DevComm,
+    data_windows: tuple,
+    scale_windows: tuple,
+    metadata: cute.Tensor,
+    requests: cute.Tensor,
+    peers: cute.Tensor,
+    output: cute.Tensor,
+    rows: cutlass.Int64,
+    data_words: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    scale_words: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    local_requests: cutlass.Constexpr,
+    stream: cuda.CUstream,
+):
+    _lookup_kernel(
+        comm,
+        data_windows,
+        scale_windows,
+        metadata,
+        requests,
+        peers,
+        output,
+        rows,
+        data_words,
+        scale_words,
+        local_requests,
+    ).launch(grid=((rows + 3) // 4, 1, 1), block=(128, 1, 1), stream=stream)

+
+class EngramDeviceTransport:
+    """One LSA/GIN transport per explicit row-shard group, shared by its tables."""
+
+    def __init__(self, group):
+        version = nccl.get_version()
+        if version.nccl4py < Version("0.6.0") or version.libnccl is None:
+            raise ImportError(
+                "Engram symmetric requires nccl4py >= 0.6.0 and its NCCL device bitcode"
+            )
+        if version.libnccl.version != version.nccl_bindings:
+            raise ImportError(
+                "Engram symmetric requires matching NCCL runtime, NCCL4Py headers and device "
+                f"bitcode; got runtime {version.libnccl.version}, headers {version.nccl_bindings}"
+            )
+        self.group = group
+        # Megatron uses None for a local, unsharded table, not WORLD.
+        self.rank = torch.distributed.get_rank(group) if group is not None else 0
+        self.size = torch.distributed.get_world_size(group) if group is not None else 1
+        self.channels = min(4, self.size)
+        self.comm = None
+        self.device_view = None
+        self.tables = {}
+        self.lookup_kernels = {}
+
+    def _initialize(self, device, workspace_bytes):
+        if self.comm is not None:
+            if device != self.buffer.device:
+                raise ValueError("An Engram transport cannot span multiple local CUDA devices")
+            return
+        unique_id = [nccl.get_unique_id() if self.rank == 0 else None]
+        if self.size > 1:
+            torch.distributed.broadcast_object_list(
+                unique_id,
+                src=torch.distributed.get_global_rank(self.group, 0),
+                group=self.group,
+                device=device,
+            )
+        with torch.cuda.device(device):
+            self.comm = nccl.Communicator.init(
+                nranks=self.size, rank=self.rank, unique_id=unique_id[0]
+            )
+            if not self.comm.device_api_support:
+                raise RuntimeError("This NCCL communicator does not support the device API")
+            self.has_gin = self.comm.team_lsa.n_ranks != self.size
+            if self.has_gin and self.comm.gin_type == nccl.NcclGinType.NONE:
+                raise RuntimeError("Engram shards cross LSA domains, but NCCL has no GIN transport")
+            self.dev_comm = self.comm.create_dev_comm(
+                nccl.NCCLDevCommRequirements(
+                    barrier_count=1 if self.has_gin else 0,
+                    lsa_barrier_count=1,
+                    gin_connection_type=(
+                        nccl.NcclGinConnectionType.FULL
+                        if self.has_gin
+                        else nccl.NcclGinConnectionType.NONE
+                    ),
+                    gin_signal_count=self.size * 4 if self.has_gin else 0,
+                    gin_context_count=1 if self.has_gin else 0,
+                )
+            )
+            flags_bytes = self.size * 4 * 8
+            self.slot_bytes = (
+                (workspace_bytes - flags_bytes) // (2 * (self.size + self.channels)) // 256 * 256
+            )
+            if self.slot_bytes <= 0:
+                raise ValueError("Engram workspace cannot hold two receive slots per shard")
+            self.flags_offset = self.slot_bytes * 2 * (self.size + self.channels)
+            self.buffer = nccl_torch.empty(workspace_bytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+            self.buffer[self.flags_offset : self.flags_offset + flags_bytes].zero_()
+            self.sequence = torch.zeros(self.size * 4, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+            self.window = self.comm.register_window(self.buffer)
+            if not self.window.is_valid:
+                raise RuntimeError("NCCL did not register the Engram workspace")
+            self.device_view, self.window_view = nc.DevComm(self.dev_comm), nc.Window(self.window)
+        # Publish initialized flags before another GPU can touch this workspace.
+        self.barrier()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _stream():
+        return cuda.CUstream(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)
+
+    def barrier(self):
+        """Publish parameter updates or finish all remote reads before reuse."""
+        _table_barrier(self.device_view, self.has_gin, self._stream())
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def exchange(
+        self,
+        source,
+        recv_splits,
+        send_splits,
+        plan,
+        workspace_bytes,
+        *,
+        remote_only=False,
+        output=None,
+    ):
+        """Exchange opaque rows with bounded slots and no host chunk loop."""
+        if not source.is_cuda or source.ndim < 2:
+            raise ValueError("Engram symmetric requires CUDA row tensors")
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            raise RuntimeError("Engram communication must remain outside CUDA Graph capture")
+        if (
+            plan is None
+            or plan.peer_counts[self.rank].tolist() != send_splits
+            or plan.peer_counts[:, self.rank].tolist() != recv_splits
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Engram exchange plan does not match its peer splits")
+        if sum(send_splits) != source.shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError("Engram input splits must cover every input row")
+        self._initialize(source.device, workspace_bytes)
+        source = source.contiguous()
+        row_bytes = math.prod(source.shape[1:]) * source.element_size()
+        if row_bytes <= 0 or row_bytes > self.slot_bytes:
+            raise ValueError("Engram workspace cannot hold a complete row per peer/slot")
+        if output is None:
+            output = source.new_empty((sum(recv_splits), *source.shape[1:]))
+        if (
+            output.shape != (sum(recv_splits), *source.shape[1:])
+            or output.dtype != source.dtype
+            or not output.is_contiguous()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Engram output must match the receive shape and dtype")
+        if plan.max_rows == 0:
+            return output
+        aligned = source.data_ptr() % 4 == output.data_ptr() % 4 == row_bytes % 4 == 0
+        word_dtype = torch.int32 if aligned else torch.uint8
+        word_bytes = torch.empty((), dtype=word_dtype).element_size()
+        counts = torch.tensor([send_splits, recv_splits], dtype=torch.int64)
+        starts = counts.cumsum(1) - counts
+        splits = torch.stack((starts[0], counts[0], starts[1], counts[1]), dim=1).to(source.device)
+        _exchange(
+            self.device_view,
+            self.window_view,
+            _rows_tensor(source.view(word_dtype).reshape(-1)),
+            _rows_tensor(output.view(word_dtype).reshape(-1)),
+            from_dlpack(splits),
+            from_dlpack(self.sequence),
+            cutlass.Int64(self.slot_bytes),
+            cutlass.Int64(self.flags_offset),
+            cutlass.Int64(row_bytes // word_bytes),
+            self.channels,
+            self.has_gin,
+            remote_only,
+            self._stream(),
+        )
+        return output
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _storage_view(tensor):
+        storage = tensor.untyped_storage()
+        stride = tensor.stride(0) * tensor.element_size()
+        if not storage.nbytes():
+            # Empty owners must still participate in collective registration.
+            return nccl.mem_alloc(256, device=tensor.device), 0, stride
+
+        address = storage.data_ptr()
+        with torch.cuda.device(tensor.device):
+            status, allocation, size = cuda.cuMemGetAddressRange(address)
+        if status != cuda.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Cannot query Engram CUDA allocation at {address:#x}: {status}")
+        allocation, size = int(allocation), int(size)
+        if not allocation <= address < allocation + size:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Invalid CUDA allocation range for Engram storage at {address:#x}")
+
+        # A PyTorch storage can itself be an unaligned allocator suballocation.
+        # Start at the CUDA allocation base: NCCL's LSA pointer calculation uses
+        # the local window's allocation offset for every peer, so merely rounding
+        # to 4 KiB is insufficient when that offset differs between ranks.
+        # The storage may span multiple VMM segments; NCCL traverses those itself.
+        view = Buffer.from_handle(
+            allocation, address + storage.nbytes() - allocation, owner=storage
+        )
+        # The borrowed buffer keeps the original allocation alive, without copying
+        # the table or taking ownership of the aligned address.
+        return view, tensor.data_ptr() - allocation, stride
+
+    def _register_tables(self, key, data, scales):
+        signatures = tuple(
+            (
+                tensor.untyped_storage().data_ptr(),
+                tensor.untyped_storage().nbytes(),
+                tensor.data_ptr(),
+                tensor.stride(0) * tensor.element_size(),
+            )
+            for tensor in (*data, *scales)
+        )
+        cached = self.tables.get(key)
+        changed = cached is None or cached[0] != signatures
+        descriptors, error = [], None
+        try:
+            # Reuse allocation queries and borrowed buffers until storage changes.
+            descriptors = (
+                [self._storage_view(tensor) for tensor in (*data, *scales)]
+                if changed
+                else cached[2]
+            )
+        except Exception as exc:
+            error = f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}"
+        # A collective decision is necessary: only one shard may have had its
+        # parameter storage replaced by an optimizer/DDP buffer refresh.
+        info = (changed, [(offset, stride) for _, offset, stride in descriptors], error)
+        gathered = [info]
+        if self.size > 1:
+            gathered = [None] * self.size
+            torch.distributed.all_gather_object(gathered, info, group=self.group)
+        errors = [f"row rank {rank}: {item[2]}" for rank, item in enumerate(gathered) if item[2]]
+        if errors:
+            raise RuntimeError("Cannot prepare Engram table windows: " + "; ".join(errors))
+        if any(item[0] for item in gathered):
+            self.barrier()
+            torch.cuda.current_stream().synchronize()
+            if cached is not None:
+                for window in cached[1]:
+                    window.close()
+                self.tables.pop(key)
+            windows = []
+            try:
+                for view, _, _ in descriptors:
+                    window = self.comm.register_window(view)
+                    if not window.is_valid:
+                        raise RuntimeError("NCCL returned an invalid table window")
+                    windows.append(window)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                for window in windows:
+                    window.close()
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    "Engram direct lookup requires registerable CUDA table storage. Use VMM "
+                    "allocations (PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True) or an "
+                    "NCCL allocator; the backend never copies the entire table."
+                ) from exc
+            metadata = []
+            for table in range(len(data)):
+                metadata.append(
+                    [
+                        [*item[1][table], *(item[1][table + len(data)] if scales else (0, 0))]
+                        for item in gathered
+                    ]
+                )
+            aligned = all(value % 4 == 0 for table in metadata for peer in table for value in peer)
+            metadata = torch.tensor(metadata, dtype=torch.int64, device=data[0].device)
+            # Keep registered allocations alive even when an optimizer replaces a view.
+            cached = (signatures, windows, descriptors, metadata, aligned)
+        self.tables[key] = cached
+        return cached[1], cached[3], cached[4]
+
+    @torch.no_grad()
+    def lookup(self, key, data, scales, requests, send, recv, plans, workspace_bytes):
+        """Read LSA rows directly and exchange only cross-domain requests/results."""
+        if not requests.is_cuda:
+            raise ValueError("Engram symmetric requires CUDA tensors")
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            raise RuntimeError("Engram communication must remain outside CUDA Graph capture")
+        self._initialize(requests.device, workspace_bytes)
+        if any(tensor.ndim != 2 or tensor.stride(1) != 1 for tensor in (*data, *scales)):
+            raise ValueError("Engram direct lookup requires row-major table data and scales")
+        windows, metadata, aligned = self._register_tables(key, data, scales)
+        data_bytes = data[0].shape[1] * data[0].element_size()
+        scale_bytes = data[0].shape[1] // 32 if scales else 0
+        row_bytes = data_bytes + scale_bytes
+        dtype = torch.int32 if aligned and data_bytes % 4 == scale_bytes % 4 == 0 else torch.uint8
+        word_bytes = torch.empty((), dtype=dtype).element_size()
+        output = torch.empty((sum(send), row_bytes), dtype=torch.uint8, device=requests.device)
+        data_windows = tuple(nc.Window(window) for window in windows[: len(data)])
+        scale_windows = tuple(nc.Window(window) for window in windows[len(data) :])
+
+        def gather(ids, splits, target, local_requests):
+            if not ids.shape[0]:
+                return
+            peers = torch.repeat_interleave(
+                torch.arange(self.size, device=ids.device),
+                torch.tensor(splits, dtype=torch.int64, device=ids.device),
+                output_size=ids.shape[0],
+            )
+            tensor_args = (
+                from_dlpack(metadata),
+                _rows_tensor(ids),
+                _rows_tensor(peers),
+                _rows_tensor(target.view(dtype).reshape(-1)),
+                cutlass.Int64(ids.shape[0]),
+            )
+            signature = (len(data), dtype, data_bytes, scale_bytes, local_requests)
+            if signature not in self.lookup_kernels:
+                # Auto-JIT tries to extract device IR from host Window objects
+                # nested in tuples (and rejects an empty scale tuple). Compile
+                # with NCCL's type-only arguments, then pass live handles to the
+                # executable. Row counts and table addresses remain dynamic.
+                self.lookup_kernels[signature] = cute.compile(
+                    _lookup,
+                    make_fake_dev_comm(),
+                    tuple(make_fake_window() for _ in data_windows),
+                    tuple(make_fake_window() for _ in scale_windows),
+                    make_fake_tensor(cutlass.Int64, metadata.shape, metadata.stride()),
+                    make_fake_tensor(cutlass.Int64, (cute.sym_int64(),), (1,)),
+                    make_fake_tensor(cutlass.Int64, (cute.sym_int64(),), (1,)),
+                    make_fake_tensor(
+                        cutlass.Int32 if word_bytes == 4 else cutlass.Uint8,
+                        (cute.sym_int64(),),
+                        (1,),
+                    ),
+                    cutlass.Int64(0),
+                    data_bytes // word_bytes,
+                    scale_bytes // word_bytes,
+                    local_requests,
+                    make_fake_stream(),
+                )
+            self.lookup_kernels[signature](
+                self.device_view, data_windows, scale_windows, *tensor_args, self._stream()
+            )
+
+        self.barrier()
+        gather(requests, send, output, True)
+        if self.has_gin:
+            remote_ids = self.exchange(
+                requests, recv, send, plans[0], workspace_bytes, remote_only=True
+            )
+            packed = output.new_empty((sum(recv), row_bytes))

+class QKVLayout:
+    """Logical row layout for a packed attention projection weight.
+
+    Both split-shape tuples describe boundaries within one logical group. Standard fused QKV
+    uses one group per query group; MLA up-projections use one group per attention head.
+
+    Projection-level Muon combines the same entry of ``projection_split_shapes`` across all
+    groups into one Newton-Schulz matrix. Per-head Muon instead repeats
+    ``per_head_split_shapes`` for every group and processes every resulting slice independently.
+    For example, two MLA heads with content/positional widths ``(2, 2)`` produce two 4-row
+    projection-level matrices, but four independent 2-row per-head matrices.
+    """
+
+    num_groups: int
+    projection_split_shapes: tuple[int, ...]
+    per_head_split_shapes: tuple[int, ...]
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_transformer_config(cls, config: TransformerConfig) -> Self:
+        """Build the fused QKV row layout described by a transformer config."""
+        assert config.num_query_groups is not None
+        assert config.kv_channels is not None
+        num_query_heads_per_group = config.num_attention_heads // config.num_query_groups
+        projection_split_shapes = [num_query_heads_per_group * config.kv_channels]
+        per_head_split_shapes = [config.kv_channels] * num_query_heads_per_group
+        if getattr(config, "attention_output_gate", False):
+            projection_split_shapes.append(num_query_heads_per_group * config.kv_channels)
+            per_head_split_shapes += [config.kv_channels] * num_query_heads_per_group
+        projection_split_shapes += [config.kv_channels, config.kv_channels]
+        per_head_split_shapes += [config.kv_channels, config.kv_channels]
+        return cls(
+            num_groups=config.num_query_groups,
+            projection_split_shapes=tuple(projection_split_shapes),
+            per_head_split_shapes=tuple(per_head_split_shapes),
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_mla_head_components(cls, num_heads: int, component_widths: tuple[int, ...]) -> Self:
+        """Build an MLA up-projection layout from one head's component widths.
+
+        Each group is one attention head. Projection-level Muon aggregates each component
+        across all heads, whereas per-head Muon processes each component of each head
+        independently.
+        """
+        return cls(
+            num_groups=num_heads,
+            projection_split_shapes=component_widths,
+            per_head_split_shapes=component_widths,

+    class _GroupedWeightView:
+        """Give TE a grouped storage view without replacing its optimizer parameter.

+        All operation methods stay bound to the real owner, including quantizer

+        def __init__(self, operation) -> None:

+        @property

+            if grouped.requires_grad != weight.requires_grad:
+                grouped.requires_grad_(weight.requires_grad)

+
+        def __getattr__(self, name):
+            return getattr(self.operation, name)
+
+    class DSv4BatchedLinear(BatchedLinear):
+        """Keep one [groups * out_features, in_features] parameter for the optimizer.
+
+        A grouped view supplies TE's batched GEMM geometry without changing the
+        parameter or its quantized storage. The 2D parameter preserves Muon's
+        matrix classification and whole-matrix update semantics.
+        """
+
+        def __init__(self, batch_size: int, in_features: int, out_features: int, **kwargs) -> None:
+            if kwargs.get('bias', False):
+                raise ValueError('DSv4 grouped output projection does not support bias.')
+            kwargs['bias'] = False
+            # Deferred meta initialization may occur after quantized_model_init exits.
+            self._preserve_high_precision_init_val = (
+                FP8GlobalStateManager.with_high_precision_init_val()
+            )
+            super().__init__(batch_size, in_features, out_features, **kwargs)
+            # Meta-device construction defers reset_parameters until materialization.
+            self._flatten_weight()
+
+        def _flatten_weight(self) -> None:
+            weight = self.weight
+            if weight.ndim == 2:
+                return
+            flat_shape = (self.batch_size * self.out_features, self.in_features)
+            self.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
+                weight.reshape(flat_shape), requires_grad=weight.requires_grad
+            )
+            # Preserve the high-precision initialization used to create optimizer masters.
+            if hasattr(weight, '_high_precision_init_val'):
+                initial_value = weight._high_precision_init_val
+                self.weight._high_precision_init_val = (
+                    initial_value.reshape(flat_shape) if initial_value is not None else None
+                )
+
+        def reset_parameters(self) -> None:
+            """Initialize using the existing TE recipe, then expose a single matrix."""
+            init_method = self._init_method
+            initial_value = None
+            preserve_initial_value = (
+                self._with_quantized_weight and self._preserve_high_precision_init_val
+            )
+
+            def initialize(weight):
+                nonlocal initial_value
+                result = init_method(weight)
+                # TE's operation currently omits the high-precision initializer
+                # retained by its Linear modules for optimizer master weights.
+                initial_value = weight.detach().clone()
+                return result
+
+            if preserve_initial_value:
+                self._init_method = initialize

+                super().reset_parameters()
+            finally:
+                self._init_method = init_method
+            self._flatten_weight()
+            if initial_value is not None:
+                self.weight._high_precision_init_val = initial_value.reshape(self.weight.shape)

+            expected = (self.batch_size * self.out_features, self.in_features)
+            if tuple(self.weight.shape) != expected:
+                raise ValueError(f'DSv4 grouped weight must have shape {expected}.')

+                if self.weight._with_gemm_swizzled_scales:
+                    raise ValueError('DSv4 BatchedLinear requires compact MXFP8 scales.')
+
+        def op_forward(self, ctx, input_, **kwargs):
+            """Use TE's native quantization and capture path with a zero-copy 3D view."""
+            return BatchedLinear.op_forward(_GroupedWeightView(self), ctx, input_, **kwargs)
+
+        def op_backward(self, ctx, grad_output):
+            """Return flat gradients while TE accumulates directly into flat main_grad."""
+            grad_input, (grad_weight,) = super().op_backward(ctx, grad_output)
+            if grad_weight is not None:
+                grad_weight = grad_weight.reshape(self.weight.shape)
+            return grad_input, [grad_weight]
+

+The equivalent backend-specific CLI value is a JSON object:
+
+```bash
+--moe-megakernel-backend mok --moe-megakernel-backend-config '{"fwd_num_comm_sms": 40, "bwd_num_comm_sms": 28}'
+```
+
+MOK is an optional dependency, imported only when the backend is selected. The ARM64 development
+image already installs the supported
+[MCore integration snapshot](https://github.com/QiZhangNV/mixture-of-kittens/tree/7a8cfb7fdd96a1cfba506caf4756c6c86073399a)
+through `docker/common/install_mok.sh`. Use that image or its installation helper to retain the
+supported dependency and Blackwell build targets. The AMD64 image skips MOK because its H100
+target is unsupported.
+
+| Area | Current MOK support |
+|------|---------------------|
+| GPU architecture | NVIDIA Blackwell SM100/SM103; upstream integration validated on GB300 |
+| Routed precision | BF16, or MXFP8 with `fp8_param=True` and native TE rowwise/columnwise payloads and scales |
+| Shared experts | Required; BF16; same intermediate size as routed experts; optional BF16 sigmoid output gate via `moe_shared_expert_gate` |
+| Activation | SwiGLU, without a linear offset or tanh clamp |
+| Routed weight layout | Per-expert non-single weights, or single-grouped weights with `moe_use_grouped_tensor=True` and Transformer Engine 2.14+ |
+| Parallelism | TP=1, expert TP=1, EP in {1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64}; each EP group must fit within one NVLink domain supporting PyTorch symmetric memory and multicast |
+| Shapes | Hidden and expert intermediate sizes divisible by 256; at least 512 local tokens per rank, divisible by 256; identical token, hidden, and top-k shapes across EP ranks |
+| Recomputation | Whole-MoE activation recompute |
+| CUDA Graph | Full-iteration capture |
+| Checkpointing | Save/resume with unchanged backend, weight layout, and parallel configuration |
+
+Wgrad GEMMs accumulate in FP32. The destination `main_grad` dtype selects the reduction-store
+precision: FP32 retains FP32 contributions, while BF16 rounds each contribution before adding it
+to the BF16 gradient buffer. This is independent of the BF16 shared-expert weight dtype.
+The pinned MOK entrypoint requires shared and routed expert main-grad buffers to use the same dtype.
+The optional shared output gate aliases the native shared-expert parameter and accumulates into
+its FP32 or BF16 `main_grad`. It supports Qwen3.5's gated shared-expert MoE without changing native
+parameter ownership or checkpoint keys; the GDN and attention layers retain their existing paths.
+
+With `reuse_grad_buf_for_mxfp8_param_ag`, MCore completes parameter all-gather, requantizes into
+native TE storage, and clears the staging buffer before MOK runs. Single-grouped MXFP8 parameters
+require this mode in the current MCore buffer implementation. MOK aliases the native payloads
+and refreshes its converted scale buffers once per optimizer iteration. The adapter requires
+both native weight layouts; TE's `post_all_gather_processing` is not an MXFP8 capability check.
+
+Per-layer whole-layer capture is distinct from `cuda_graph_impl=full_iteration`. Supporting
+per-layer MOK replay needs saved-state stashing or a recompute path for pending microbatches;
+static input token counts alone do not establish that lifecycle.
+
+The current backend requires grouped experts and fused gradient accumulation. It does not support
+linear biases, applying router probabilities to expert inputs, MCore EP 1F1B overlap or delayed
+wgrad, native shared-expert overlap, shared-expert-only
+recompute, latent MoE, GTP weight rematerialization, shortcut MoE, inference-optimized layers,
+partial MoE CUDA Graph replay, MCore expert-input
+capacity padding, FC1 GLU-interleaved weights, or checkpoint conversion between physical weight
+layouts.

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""Construction entry point for MoE megakernel backends."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from contextlib import nullcontext
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+from torch import nn
+from torch.distributed import ProcessGroup
+
+from megatron.core.transformer.moe.megakernel.backend import MegakernelBackend
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import TransformerConfig
+
+
+def build_megakernel_backend(
+    *,
+    config: TransformerConfig,
+    ep_group: ProcessGroup,
+    routed_experts: nn.Module,
+    shared_experts: nn.Module,
+    num_local_experts: int,
+) -> MegakernelBackend:
+    """Build the configured megakernel backend.
+
+    Backend imports are deliberately lazy so ordinary MCore MoE configurations
+    do not acquire optional megakernel dependencies.
+    """
+    backend = config.moe_megakernel_backend
+    if backend == "mok":
+        from megatron.core.transformer.moe.megakernel.mok.backend import MoKMegakernel
+
+        return MoKMegakernel(
+            config=config,
+            ep_group=ep_group,
+            routed_experts=routed_experts,
+            shared_experts=shared_experts,
+            num_local_experts=num_local_experts,
+        )
+    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MoE megakernel backend: {backend!r}")
+
+
+def prepare_megakernel_shared_expert_config(config: TransformerConfig) -> TransformerConfig:
+    """Return the config used to construct backend-compatible shared experts."""
+    backend = config.moe_megakernel_backend
+    if backend is None:
+        return config
+    if backend == "mok":
+        from megatron.core.transformer.moe.megakernel.mok.weights import (
+            prepare_shared_expert_config,
+        )
+
+        return prepare_shared_expert_config(config)
+    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MoE megakernel backend: {backend!r}")
+
+
+def megakernel_shared_expert_init_context(config: TransformerConfig):
+    """Return the backend-specific context used to construct shared experts."""
+    backend = config.moe_megakernel_backend
+    if backend is None:
+        return nullcontext()
+    if backend == "mok":
+        from megatron.core.fp8_utils import get_fp8_disabled_context
+
+        # MOK consumes native BF16 shared weights. Disable any model-wide TE
+        # fp8_model_init context while the authoritative MCore module is built.
+        return get_fp8_disabled_context(config, is_init=True)
+    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported MoE megakernel backend: {backend!r}")

+        fc2_ref = shared.linear_fc2.weight

+        so descriptors keep their addresses. It does not requantize the weights.

+        modules (``TEGroupedLinear`` etc.). ``torch.nn.Module._apply`` moves traceable wrapper
+        subclasses (TE quantized tensors such as ``MXFP8Tensor``) with
+        ``torch.utils.swap_tensors``, which exchanges the parameter object's whole ``__dict__``.
+        TE's own modules re-attach the externally attached state afterwards
+        (``TransformerEngineBaseModule._apply``), but this plain module's visit of the *same*
+        object (e.g. during ``model.cuda()``) swaps it again and nothing restores it, so mcore's
+        ``allreduce`` / ``partition_dim`` / ``tensor_model_parallel`` stamps and TE's
+        ``_high_precision_init_val`` are lost. DDP / the layer-wise optimizer then treat the routed
+        experts as data-parallel replicas (grads all-reduced across EP ranks, master weights
+        sharded over dp_cp, identical experts across the EP group). Mirror TE's fix here.
+        """

+            name: (param, dict(param.__dict__))
+            for name, param in self._parameters.items()
+            if param is not None
+        }
+        out = super()._apply(*args, **kwargs)
+        for name, (old_param, attrs) in snapshots.items():
+            new_param = self._parameters.get(name)
+            if new_param is None:

+                if key in new_param.__dict__:

+                if isinstance(value, MethodType) and value.__self__ is old_param:
+                    value = MethodType(value.__func__, new_param)
+                setattr(new_param, key, value)

+@triton.jit
+def _routing_map_to_indices_kernel(
+    probs_ptr,
+    routing_map_ptr,
+    probs_indices_ptr,
+    indices_ptr,
+    num_experts: tl.constexpr,
+    topk: tl.constexpr,
+    num_experts_block_size: tl.constexpr,
+    topk_block_size: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Compact one dense routing-map row and gather its router probabilities."""
+    token_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    expert_offsets = tl.arange(0, num_experts_block_size)
+    expert_mask = expert_offsets < num_experts
+    row_offset = token_idx * num_experts
+    routed = tl.load(routing_map_ptr + row_offset + expert_offsets, mask=expert_mask, other=0) != 0
+    route_positions = tl.cumsum(routed.to(tl.int32), axis=0) - 1
+    topk_offsets = tl.arange(0, topk_block_size)
+    topk_mask = topk_offsets < topk
+    output_row_offset = token_idx * topk
+    tl.store(indices_ptr + output_row_offset + topk_offsets, -1, mask=topk_mask)
+    tl.store(probs_indices_ptr + output_row_offset + topk_offsets, 0.0, mask=topk_mask)
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    valid_route = routed & expert_mask & (route_positions < topk)
+    routed_probs = tl.load(probs_ptr + row_offset + expert_offsets, mask=valid_route, other=0.0).to(
+        tl.float32
+    )
+    tl.store(indices_ptr + output_row_offset + route_positions, expert_offsets, mask=valid_route)
+    tl.store(
+        probs_indices_ptr + output_row_offset + route_positions, routed_probs, mask=valid_route
+    )

+@triton.jit
+def _routing_map_to_indices_backward_kernel(
+    grad_probs_indices_ptr,
+    indices_ptr,
+    grad_probs_ptr,
+    num_experts: tl.constexpr,
+    topk: tl.constexpr,
+    num_experts_block_size: tl.constexpr,
+    topk_block_size: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Scatter compact router-weight gradients back into the dense probability row."""
+    token_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    expert_offsets = tl.arange(0, num_experts_block_size)
+    expert_mask = expert_offsets < num_experts
+    grad_probs_row_offset = token_idx * num_experts
+    tl.store(grad_probs_ptr + grad_probs_row_offset + expert_offsets, 0.0, mask=expert_mask)
+    tl.debug_barrier()
+    topk_offsets = tl.arange(0, topk_block_size)
+    topk_mask = topk_offsets < topk
+    compact_row_offset = token_idx * topk
+    indices = tl.load(indices_ptr + compact_row_offset + topk_offsets, mask=topk_mask, other=-1)
+    valid_route = topk_mask & (indices >= 0) & (indices < num_experts)
+    grad_probs_indices = tl.load(
+        grad_probs_indices_ptr + compact_row_offset + topk_offsets, mask=valid_route, other=0.0
+    )
+    tl.store(grad_probs_ptr + grad_probs_row_offset + indices, grad_probs_indices, mask=valid_route)

+class RoutingMapToIndices(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Compact a dense routing map into fixed-width expert indices and probabilities.
+    Unlike torch.topk(probs), this operation treats routing_map as the
+    authoritative route set. Each row is compacted in increasing expert-index
+    order. Rows with fewer than topk routes are padded with -1 indices
+    and zero probabilities. The backward pass scatters router-weight gradients
+    into the corresponding positions of the dense probability tensor.

+    def forward(ctx, probs, routing_map, topk):
+        """Compact authoritative dense routes into fixed-width MOK inputs."""
+        if not HAVE_TRITON:
+            raise RuntimeError("routing_map_to_mok_inputs requires Triton")
+        if probs.ndim != 2 or routing_map.ndim != 2:
+            raise ValueError("probs and routing_map must both be two-dimensional")
+        if probs.shape != routing_map.shape:
+            raise ValueError("probs and routing_map must have the same shape")
+        if not probs.is_cuda or not routing_map.is_cuda or probs.device != routing_map.device:
+            raise ValueError("probs and routing_map must be CUDA tensors on the same device")
+        if not probs.is_contiguous() or not routing_map.is_contiguous():
+            raise ValueError("probs and routing_map must be contiguous")
+        if probs.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
+            raise TypeError("probs must have dtype float16, bfloat16, or float32")
+        if type(topk) is not int or topk <= 0 or topk > probs.shape[1]:
+            raise ValueError("topk must be a positive integer no greater than num_experts")
+        num_tokens, num_experts = probs.shape
+        probs_indices = torch.empty((num_tokens, topk), dtype=torch.float32, device=probs.device)
+        indices = torch.empty((num_tokens, topk), dtype=torch.int32, device=probs.device)
+        if num_tokens > 0:
+            num_experts_block_size = triton.next_power_of_2(num_experts)
+            topk_block_size = triton.next_power_of_2(topk)
+            num_warps = 4 if num_experts_block_size <= 512 else 8
+            _routing_map_to_indices_kernel[(num_tokens,)](
+                probs,
+                routing_map,
+                probs_indices,
+                indices,
+                num_experts=num_experts,
+                topk=topk,
+                num_experts_block_size=num_experts_block_size,
+                topk_block_size=topk_block_size,
+                num_warps=num_warps,
+            )
+        ctx.save_for_backward(indices)
+        ctx.num_experts = num_experts
+        ctx.probs_dtype = probs.dtype

+            num_experts_block_size = triton.next_power_of_2(ctx.num_experts)
+            topk_block_size = triton.next_power_of_2(topk)
+            num_warps = 4 if num_experts_block_size <= 512 else 8
+            _routing_map_to_indices_backward_kernel[(num_tokens,)](
+                grad_probs_indices.contiguous(),
+                indices,
+                grad_probs,
+                num_experts=ctx.num_experts,
+                topk=topk,
+                num_experts_block_size=num_experts_block_size,
+                topk_block_size=topk_block_size,
+                num_warps=num_warps,
+            )

+
+
+def routing_map_to_mok_inputs(
+    probs: torch.Tensor, routing_map: torch.Tensor, topk: int
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Compact an authoritative routing map into fixed-width MOK inputs.
+    Args:
+        probs: Dense router probabilities with shape [num_tokens, num_experts].
+        routing_map: Dense boolean/integer route map with the same shape as probs.
+        topk: Maximum number of valid routes emitted per token.
+    Returns:
+        A pair (probs_indices, indices) with shapes [num_tokens, topk].
+        probs_indices is float32 and indices is int32 with -1 padding.
+    """
+    return RoutingMapToIndices.apply(probs, routing_map, topk)

+def _gate_up_weight_arguments(shared_fc1: torch.Tensor, routed_fc1, intermediate_size: int):
+    """Adapt MCore-owned combined FC1 weights to MOK's gate/up API.
+
+    Shared FC1 is a dense two-dimensional parameter, so gate and up are
+    ordinary zero-copy row views. Routed FC1 may span multiple experts or
+    descriptor-backed allocations; passing the same combined payload for gate
+    and up preserves its storage metadata, and MOK applies the existing logical
+    gate/up offsets when the two arguments alias.
+    """
+    expected_rows = 2 * intermediate_size
+    if shared_fc1.ndim != 2 or shared_fc1.shape[0] != expected_rows:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "MOK shared FC1 shape mismatch: "
+            f"got {tuple(shared_fc1.shape)}, expected [{expected_rows}, hidden_size]"
+        )
+    shared_gate = shared_fc1.narrow(0, 0, intermediate_size)
+    shared_up = shared_fc1.narrow(0, intermediate_size, intermediate_size)
+    return shared_gate, shared_up, routed_fc1, routed_fc1
+

+def _gate_up_main_grad_arguments(main_grads, main_grad_storage_tables, intermediate_size: int):
+    """Adapt canonical FC1/FC2 main-grad buffers to MOK's six-buffer order."""
+    shared_fc1, routed_fc1, shared_fc2, routed_fc2 = main_grads
+    shared_gate, shared_up, routed_gate, routed_up = _gate_up_weight_arguments(
+        shared_fc1, routed_fc1, intermediate_size
+    )
+    split_main_grads = (shared_gate, routed_gate, shared_up, routed_up, shared_fc2, routed_fc2)
+    if main_grad_storage_tables is None:
+        return split_main_grads, None
+    routed_fc1_table, routed_fc2_table = main_grad_storage_tables
+    return split_main_grads, (routed_fc1_table, routed_fc1_table, routed_fc2_table)

+    @staticmethod

+        module: "MoKMegakernel",

+        router_weights: torch.Tensor,
+        top_experts: torch.Tensor,
+        shared_output_gate_weight: torch.Tensor | None,
+        *parameters: torch.Tensor,

+        from mok import functional

+        if len(parameters) != num_routed_parameters + 2:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "MOK autograd parameter count mismatch: "
+                f"got {len(parameters)}, expected {num_routed_parameters + 2}"
+            )
+        routed_parameters = parameters[:num_routed_parameters]
+        shared_fc1, shared_fc2 = parameters[num_routed_parameters:]

+            module.mok_config,
+            module.ep_group,

+            hidden_size=x.shape[1],
+            topk=top_experts.shape[1],

+        else:

+            # Non-single BF16/MXFP8 use SplitRoutedWeight objects consumed directly by MOK.
+            fc1_forward = fc1_weight_view
+            fc2_forward = fc2_weight_view

+        )

+            workspace,
+            schedule,
+            x,
+            router_weights,
+            shared_gate,
+            shared_up,
+            shared_fc2,
+            routed_gate,

+        ctx.module = module
+        ctx.workspace = workspace
+        ctx.schedule = schedule
+        ctx.forward_context = forward_context
+        ctx.routed_weight_views = (fc1_weight_view, fc2_weight_view)

+            backward_fc2 = fc2_weight_view

+            router_weights,
+            shared_gate,
+            shared_up,

+from __future__ import annotations

+import copy
+import math
+import warnings
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

+import torch
+from torch import nn

+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from megatron.core.transformer.transformer_config import TransformerConfig
+
+_SHARED_EXPERT_BF16_WARNING_EMITTED = False
+
+
+def prepare_shared_expert_config(config: TransformerConfig) -> TransformerConfig:
+    """Construct MOK shared experts as native BF16 MCore modules.
+
+    Routed experts continue to use the original model configuration. The
+    shared-only copy expresses the BF16 module configuration; the factory also
+    disables any enclosing TE FP8 model-init context during construction.
+    """
+    if not config.fp8_param:
+        return config
+
+    global _SHARED_EXPERT_BF16_WARNING_EMITTED
+    if not _SHARED_EXPERT_BF16_WARNING_EMITTED and (
+        not torch.distributed.is_initialized() or torch.distributed.get_rank() == 0
+    ):
+        warnings.warn(
+            "MOK currently computes shared experts in BF16. Shared-expert modules "
+            "will therefore be constructed with FP8 execution and FP8 parameters "
+            "disabled while routed "
+            "experts retain the model's MXFP8 parameter configuration.",
+            stacklevel=3,
+        )
+        _SHARED_EXPERT_BF16_WARNING_EMITTED = True
+
+    shared_config = copy.copy(config)
+    shared_config.fp8 = None
+    shared_config.fp8_param = False
+    return shared_config
+
+
+def _storage_view(
+    storage: torch.Tensor, shape: tuple[int, ...], *, dtype: torch.dtype, name: str
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Return a zero-copy dense view over a TE grouped backing tensor."""
+    if storage is None:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"MOK {name} requires native TE payload storage")
+    if not storage.is_cuda or not storage.is_contiguous():
+        raise RuntimeError(f"MOK {name} storage must be contiguous CUDA storage")
+    if storage.dtype != dtype:
+        if storage.dtype == torch.uint8 and dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn:
+            storage = storage.view(dtype)
+        else:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"MOK {name} storage has dtype {storage.dtype}, expected {dtype}")
+    expected_numel = 1
+    for dim in shape:
+        expected_numel *= dim
+    if storage.numel() != expected_numel:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"MOK {name} storage size mismatch: got {storage.numel()}, "
+            f"expected {expected_numel} for {shape}"
+        )
+    return storage.view(shape)
+
+
+def _single_grouped_mxfp8_scale_view(
+    param: nn.Parameter, member_attr: str, shape: tuple[int, ...], *, name: str
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Expose one single-grouped parameter's expert-major MXFP8 scale storage."""
+    from megatron.core.fp8_utils import get_grouped_quantized_members
+
+    # One TE GroupedTensor is one PyTorch Parameter, but TE exposes one quantized
+    # member view per expert; their scale views share expert-major backing storage.
+    members = get_grouped_quantized_members(param)
+    if not members or len(members) != shape[0]:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"MOK {name} expected {shape[0]} grouped members, got {len(members)}")
+
+    first = getattr(members[0], member_attr)
+    expected_numel = math.prod(shape)
+    per_expert = expected_numel // shape[0]
+    storage_ptr = first.untyped_storage().data_ptr()
+    for expert, member in enumerate(members):
+        scale = getattr(member, member_attr)
+        if (
+            tuple(scale.shape) != tuple(shape[1:])
+            or not scale.is_contiguous()
+            or scale.untyped_storage().data_ptr() != storage_ptr
+            or scale.storage_offset() != first.storage_offset() + expert * per_expert
+        ):
+            raise RuntimeError(f"MOK {name} member {expert} scale is not packed expert-major")
+
+    flat = torch.as_strided(first, (expected_numel,), (1,), storage_offset=first.storage_offset())
+    return flat.view(shape)
+

+def _swizzle_mxfp8_scale(

+            f"MOK logical scale shape mismatch: got {tuple(logical_scale.shape)}, "

+    )

+        _swizzle_mxfp8_scale(
+            column_scale,

+def _parameter_storage_attr(param: nn.Parameter, name: str) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+    """Read a TE storage attribute without materializing the logical parameter.
+
+    TE releases/wrappers have exposed native storage either directly on the
+    Parameter or on param.data, using public or private attribute names.
+    """
+    candidates = (name,) if name.startswith("_") else (name, f"_{name}")
+    for candidate in candidates:
+        value = getattr(param, candidate, None)
+        if value is not None:
+            return value

+    if data is not None:
+        for candidate in candidates:
+            value = getattr(data, candidate, None)
+            if value is not None:
+                return value
+    return None

+def dummy_weight_gradient(param: nn.Parameter) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Return a zero-allocation gradient sentinel that triggers MCore DDP hooks.
+
+    The detached tensor intentionally aliases the parameter storage; callers must
+    never read or mutate its values. This is safe only after the megakernel writes
+    the numerical gradient to ``main_grad`` and sets
+    ``grad_added_to_main_grad=True``. MCore's DDP hook then clears ``.grad``
+    without reading or accumulating this sentinel.
+    """
+    return param.detach()
+

+def main_grad_buffer(param: nn.Parameter) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Return and validate an optimizer-visible FP32 or BF16 gradient buffer."""
+    main_grad = getattr(param, "main_grad", None)
+    if main_grad is None:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "Megakernel gradient accumulation requires DDP to assign param.main_grad"
+        )
+    if main_grad.shape != param.shape:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "Megakernel weight-gradient shape mismatch: "
+            f"main_grad={tuple(main_grad.shape)}, param={tuple(param.shape)}"
+        )
+    if main_grad.dtype not in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16):
+        raise RuntimeError("Megakernel direct accumulation requires FP32 or BF16 main_grad")
+    if not main_grad.is_contiguous():
+        raise RuntimeError("Megakernel direct accumulation requires contiguous main_grad")
+    if getattr(param, "zero_out_wgrad", False):
+        raise RuntimeError("Megakernel does not support zero_out_wgrad parameters")
+    if main_grad.device != param.device:
+        raise RuntimeError("Megakernel main_grad must be on the parameter device")
+    return main_grad
+
+
+def finish_weight_gradient(param: nn.Parameter) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Mark an in-kernel accumulation complete and return a DDP hook-only grad."""
+    param.grad_added_to_main_grad = True
+    return dummy_weight_gradient(param)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("layout", ["sbhd", "thd", "thd_cp"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("heads", [2, 64])
+def test_output_rope_reconstruction(layout, dtype, heads):
+    """Preserve aliases and the NoPE prefix, including B>1 and packed CP positions."""
+    seeded()
+    cu = None if layout == "sbhd" else torch.tensor([0, 6, 6, 16], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    positions = (
+        torch.tensor([2, 3, 4, 5, 0, 1, 2, 3], device="cuda") if layout == "thd_cp" else None
+    )
+    rows = 8 if layout == "thd_cp" else 16
+    x = torch.randn(rows, heads, 512, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    grad = torch.randn_like(x)
+    angles = torch.randn(16, 32, device="cuda").repeat(1, 2)
+    cos, sin = angles.cos(), angles.sin()
+    params = OutputRopeParams(
+        cos, sin, 448, 64, cu, position_ids=positions, sbhd_batch_size=2 if cu is None else None
+    )
+    original, original_grad = x.clone(), grad.clone()
+
+    # Compare with the existing autograd path, including its exact backward arithmetic.
+    ref = x.detach().clone().requires_grad_(True)
+    ref_view = ref.view(8, 2, heads, 512) if cu is None else ref
+    expected = fused_mla_rope_out_of_place(
+        ref_view,
+        cos,
+        sin,
+        448,
+        64,
+        cu,
+        0,
+        1,
+        inverse=True,
+        remove_interleaving=True,
+        position_ids=positions,
+    ).view_as(x)
+    expected.backward(grad.clone())
+
+    def run(value, upstream):
+        # Exercise the real adapter's padded-head slice before RoPE reconstruction.
+        backend_out = value.new_zeros((rows, 64, 512))
+        backend_out[:, :heads] = value
+        lse = torch.zeros(rows, 64, device=value.device)
+        indices = torch.zeros(rows, 1, device=value.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+        with (
+            patch.object(fused_csa, "_flash_mla_sparse_fwd", return_value=(backend_out, None, lse)),
+            patch.object(fused_csa, "_get_head_padding", return_value=64),
+            patch.object(fused_csa, "_get_topk_alignment", return_value=1),
+        ):
+            rotated, _, _ = fused_csa._csa_fwd_flash_mla(
+                value, value.new_empty((rows, 512)), indices, 1.0
+            )
+        params.apply_(rotated)
+        saved = rotated.clone()
+        restored, restored_grad = undo_output_rope_for_backward(params, rotated, upstream)
+        # Forward output may still be saved by the projection, and upstream can alias another edge.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(rotated, saved, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(upstream, original_grad, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        return rotated, restored, restored_grad
+
+    actual, restored, restored_grad = run(x, grad)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(restored_grad, ref.grad, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(restored[..., :448], original[..., :448], rtol=0, atol=0)

+    tolerance = 2e-2 if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else 1e-6
+    torch.testing.assert_close(restored, original, rtol=tolerance, atol=tolerance)
+    assert_replays_bit_exact(
+        run, (x, grad), backward=False, contention=True, what="CSA output RoPE"

+
+    def forward_backward():
+        output = run(local, halo)
+        return output, *torch.autograd.grad(output, (local, halo), probe)
+
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        forward_backward()
+        forward_backward()
+    stream.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+        captured = forward_backward()
+    for shift in (0, 1):
+        sources.copy_(torch.arange(32, device="cuda").roll(shift).reshape_as(sources))
+        valid.fill_(True)
+        valid[shift::3] = False
+        expected = forward_backward()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        for actual, wanted in zip(captured, expected):
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual, wanted, rtol=0, atol=0)

+"""Replay the MCore routing adapter without requiring the optional MOK package."""
+

+from megatron.core.transformer.moe.megakernel.mok.route_adapter import routing_map_to_mok_inputs
